terms.comment: The stringed instrument of Mercury and Apollo, smaller than the cithara.
The tortoise, and so the lyre whose sounding box was a tortoise shell.
The word of classical prose, always plural there: fidibus canere, play the lyre (Cic.).

phrases.latin: asinus jacentem vīdit in prātō lyram. accessit et temptāvit chordās ungulā; sonuēre tāctae.
phrases.english: a donkey saw a lyre lying in a meadow. He went up and tried the strings with his hoof; touched, they sounded.

sources: Lewis & Short: lyra · Lewis & Short: testudo · Lewis & Short: fides
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 168.
Phaedrus from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-phaedrus).
